artworks.title: Ulysses and the Sirens
artworks.description: Waterhouse gives the singers their old vase-form back — great birds with women's faces settling on the rigging around the bound king, close enough to touch.

artworks.title: Ulysses and the Sirens
artworks.description: The Edwardian nightmare version: the singers climb over the gunwale as sea-nymphs while Ulysses strains against the mast and the rowers' sealed ears hold the ship on course.

artworks.title: Odysseus Between Scylla and Charybdis
artworks.description: The strait as pure vertigo — the hero braced on a heaving deck between the whirlpool's mouth below and the six-fold shadow falling from above.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Camerini restages the mast and the song — Odysseus bound while the crew rows past the meadow of bones.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: The miniseries keeps Circe's warnings and the strait — Sirens, Scylla's six heads, and the cattle of the Sun.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.description: Book XII remains the Western template for deadly song, the whirlpool, and the choice between two monsters.

popCulture.title: Siren
popCulture.description: The bird-women of the strait endure as the emblem of beauty that kills those who listen unbound.

popCulture.title: Scylla
popCulture.description: Six mouths above Charybdis — the monster who takes six men whenever a ship threads the strait.
